title: Salvation
english: The voice of salvation cries out, saying, 'Arise, come, my neighbor, my beautiful one, my dove, for behold the winter has passed, the rain has gone, and the flowers have appeared on the earth; the time of pruning has arrived' (Song of Solomon 2:10-12).
And there was also 'like the feet of one bringing good news, a voice of peace, proclaiming good things.'

This announcement of peace and good news is a welcome sound to those who are in danger, like the feet of one bringing good news, a voice of peace, proclaiming good things, and announcing peace to those in danger.
In contrast, the barbarian armies that destroy cities and countries make war an excuse for their lawlessness.
However, when their hope falls into the opposite, the feet of the one announcing peace to those in danger are very beautiful, and the voice of peace is a comforting sound.
The good news of peace is also proclaimed by one who is evangelizing, proclaiming good things to those who are in need of salvation.
Through Christ, we can also entrust ourselves to this kind of salvation, and in this way, someone could also entrust to us the things that are upon us, through Christ.
Moreover, it is much easier to be with him, because the Father has sent us a savior and redeemer from heaven, the Son.
A boastful tyrant, who was not content with dominating one nation, but sought to conquer the entire inhabited world, was making war unjustly, doing what he wanted to do by his own power.

He had turned away from love for God and true knowledge of God, and was polluting himself with various sins, becoming a latrine for the demonic herds, and offering worship to creation contrary to the creating God.

Some people were giving reverence to the sun, others to the moon, considering it the queen of all nature, while others were offering worship to the earth, water, air, and fire, and had fallen into such evils that they were carrying the honor and glory of divinity to the point of worshiping wooden idols.
The devil, who is a murderer, boasts and lives a life of unrest, considering cheerfulness to be an unshakeable habit.
The prophet Jeremiah condemned this behavior, saying that those who multiply what is not theirs and heavily load their yoke will face punishment (Jeremiah 48:10).

However, the Word of God, who is a counselor to God the Father, preached the time of salvation to us, saying that he was anointed to preach the gospel to the poor, to proclaim release to captives, and to give sight to the blind (Luke 4:18).
When the time of the promised help arrived, the Word of God opposed himself to the devil's evil deeds for our sake, seized the murderous tyrant, and trampled underfoot those who had been deceived.
He then said, 'Behold, I have given you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall hurt you' (Luke 10:19).

Therefore, those of us who have become lovers of piety towards God and who long to share in the glory of the saints thirst to become citizens of the city above, and we think about these things for ourselves.
Those who boast in their own achievements treat the saved as their footstools, imposing taxes and laws upon them as if they were making a confession of submission.
In contrast, those who have been redeemed through Christ have been freed from the errors of polytheism and have become rich in their relationship with God through Him.
As the blessed Paul writes, one died for all, so that the living may no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died and rose for them (Romans 14:8).
This truth was also foreshadowed in the ancient scriptures, where the law is seen as a shadow that pained the formation of truth.
God said to Moses, if you take the census of the sons of Israel and each gives a ransom for their soul to the Lord, there will be no plague among them, and there will be no plague among them.
When it comes to giving the offering to the Lord to atone for our souls, the poor person will not decrease from half of the didrachma.
This coin, with its royal stamp, is a genuine one, and it was customary for those who paid it to offer it to the Lord, not just for one person, but for two.
The tax collectors, appointed according to the law, ensured that both the rich and the poor paid the same amount, keeping the truth of the matter accurately, as God had ordained.
On one occasion, when our Savior Christ entered Capernaum, the collectors of the didrachma approached Peter and asked him why their teacher did not pay the tax.
Peter replied in the affirmative, without implying that the free one was subject to the law, or that the Son was to be treated like a servant.
Rather, he knew that the lawgiver was under the law to deliver us from its curse and to change the form of slavery to something better, making us like himself and declaring us sons of God.
As Paul writes, we did not receive a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of adoption, crying out 'Abba, Father' (Romans 8:15).
The Savior then asked Peter if the sons are exempt from paying the tax, and Peter's response led to a deeper understanding of the relationship between the law and freedom…

title: The Divine Stater and the Redemption of the Nations
english: ...From whom do the sons of the earth take census or taxes? From their own sons or from strangers?

Having said that it is necessary to gather from strangers, Christ said again: 'Therefore, the sons are free.' So that we may not offend them, going to the sea, throw a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and opening its mouth, you will find a stater.
Taking that, give it to them for me and you. Thus, the didrachma was paid for two heads.

And what is the mystery, or what kind of true beauty of the truth will we find hidden in the shadow of the law? For the true stater, the image of the great King, that is, the Son, the character and the radiance of the Father's substance, gave himself for us; and in exchange for the life of all, he made his own soul, not only to save Israel, which seems to be rich in the knowledge of the law, but also to redeem the immeasurable flock of the nations, 'having no hope,' as Paul says, and which, sick with the emptiness of all good, is delivered from the devil's greed. Therefore, the divine and heavenly stater was given for two heads.

'For we have been redeemed not with perishable silver or gold, but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and spotless, Christ.' We are debtors, then, to live in the flesh, but to the Christ who redeemed and bought us.

God, the merciful one, drove the Israelites from the unpleasantness of the Egyptians' greed, and called them toward liberty, though they were being unjustly weighed down by the yoke of slavery; bitter things, indeed, he inflicted as blows upon those who were resisting.

Because he saw them having difficulty most painfully, he was grieved by the death of the firstborn; and those who were escaping the evils and the magnitude of the unexpected disaster were barely able to leave the land to those who were being forced.
Having this happen and being accomplished, God sought an equal recompense from those who had been redeemed.
For he spoke thus to the prophet Moses: 'Consecrate to me every firstborn; every firstborn, opening every womb, among the sons of Israel, from man to beast, is mine.'

Then, explaining the reason for the law to those of Israel, the blessed Moses said: 'And it shall be when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, the way he swore to your fathers, and gives it to you, that you shall free every opening womb; the males belong to the Lord.'

And again: 'If your son asks you after these things, saying, "What is this?" you shall say to him, "In hand a mighty one brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery. Whenever Pharaoh hardened his heart against sending us away, he killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of men to the firstborn of beasts. Therefore I sacrifice to God every opening womb, the males, all the firstborn of my sons."

As God subdued the enemies and unexpectedly freed us from the tyranny of the devil, and as we owed ourselves, beloved, to repay the Benefactor with equal gifts, washing away the old imprisonments with good and most excellent waters, let us now, while advancing with upright and blameless faith shining forth and with those of noble deeds, make an offering and a sacrifice that is truly spiritual.

For it is written, 'Present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, your logical worship.' Therefore, since we are especially practicing abstinence in the present time and applying the bridle of fasting, let us also follow a manner that is meek and sober. For fasting alone will not suffice to achieve virtue, but when joined with the fragrance of good works, it will be acceptable to God and full of all praise.

But perhaps someone will say, being overcome by the reproaches of their conscience: 'Why is it that I am preoccupied with sins and have a difficult burden of transgressions? What words shall I use toward the judge of all? Or what kind of defense shall any of us use against these things?' The judgment is inescapable; for the judge knows all and is unfathomable. Such a person will hear: 'You have rightly been convicted of the curse that belongs to those who love sin, but let the writings of Paul free you from these terrors.'

'Being dead in our transgressions and sins, in which we once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now working in the sons of disobedience, in which we also all once conducted ourselves in the desires of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of the thoughts; and we were by nature children of wrath, as the rest. But God, being rich in mercy, because of his great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in transgressions, made us alive together with Christ.'
For as the Savior himself has said, 'For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in him may not perish but have eternal life.'
'Shall we then, since he has become a man, be ignorant of the Master?'

title: Christology and Fasting
english: Do we not recognize the Word proceeding from God the Father, and shall we not worship Emmanuel? Away with such absurdity!

For those who have dared to think this way out of ignorance, denying the Master who purchased them, they shall hear the prophet saying, 'Go to the light of your fire, and to the flame by which you burned' (Isaiah 50:11).
Wisdom will also reprove them, saying, 'Woe to those who abandon the straight paths to walk in paths of darkness' (Proverbs 2:13).
But we, having provided a track for the diverted, walk the straight path, following the God-breathed writings.

Even though He became man through us and for us, I do not worship Him as having become merely in a man, but as a man who has become a self-refuge, for as the blessed John says, and as nature itself has testified regarding these things, 'The Word became flesh, and dwelt among us' (John 1:14).
We say that the Word became flesh, yet He did not withdraw into the nature of the flesh, for this is a stumbling block, and an alien thing to the dignity of one becoming God.

However, because He has indeed been born of a woman and has become a perfect man according to us, He is entirely conjoined in nature, but I say this union is through intellect and reason, surpassing human understanding.

The Mediator of God and men has used natural language to weave together the homogeneity of the two through Himself, for He leaped from the essence of God and the Father as God, and He took hold of us as He became man; yet He would not slip from being God because of the human nature.

But He is also thus God, not allowing the flesh to conquer the divinity that surpasses all things, but rather recovering into His own glory that which was assumed, for even the wise John, although born of a woman, knowing the truth, says that He is not from below, nor from the earth, but rather from above: 'For He who comes from above is above all' (John 3:31).
Now, scattering as far as possible the coarse things of the unbelievers and their cold myths, we must recognize our own Lord, and acknowledge that He has become man.

For the Jews, those talents who had ignored the mystery of piety, instead of pursuing Him, had released Him unpowerfully through their ignorance, saying: 'We are not stoning you for a bad work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God' (John 10:33).

Let us not contend in such a manner, for He did not, being a man, ascend into the glory of divinity; rather, being God by nature, He became man, and where else has He emptied Himself, according to the Scriptures (Philippians 2:7)?
God, existing, has become man; for He has been made God, not at all by being a man, and because of this, it is proper to worship, even if one thinks in terms of the flesh.
For the blessed one sang, as David did: 'The God will visibly come; our God, and He will not be silent' (Psalm 98:9).
And the law-giving Thomas, having felt the marks of the nails and having recognized the rest as God, worshipped, saying: 'My Lord and my God' (John 20:28).

And the Divine is indeed unascended and invisible; but He arrived visibly, not as if the Word were another from His own flesh and the temple from the Virgin, but as being understood as one with them, for it is manifest by virtue of union, according to which it is said that He has become flesh.

The Jews dishonored Him, even though they were speaking clearly: 'He who believes in me has eternal life' (John 6:47); and, 'I am the light of the world' (John 8:12); and, 'I am the resurrection and the life' (John 11:25).
But having calculated nothing of these things, they turned to conquer through rage and envy, and having died, they crucified Him, for it was not possible for the bonds of death to hold life.
For He has been raised from the dead, having plundered Hades, and having said to those in bonds: 'Come out' (Isaiah 49:9), and to those in the darkness: 'Be revealed' (Isaiah 58:8).

Having made the return to life possible for human nature, having made Himself manifest to the holy disciples, and having established them as mystagogues of the inhabited world, and having commanded baptism into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, He ascended to the Father—a first-fruit, just as something and an offering of the sleeping ones—to the spirits appearing above, so that He might establish the heaven as a foundation for us as well.
And indeed He spoke to the holy disciples: 'I will go and prepare a place for you (John 14:2); and I will come again and take you to myself (John 14:3).'
So that where I am, there you may also be with me (John 14:3).

Therefore, as we celebrate all these things, we must necessarily purify ourselves through toil and by fasting, deadening the flesh and, more importantly, the pleasures that arise in and from the flesh.
We do this so that, being purified, we may be joined to the Holy God through the Mediator, Christ, and thus manifest ourselves as worthy of the brightness of the saints.

Let us add to our fasting the performance of good works: let us complete the needs of widows, visit orphans, break bread for the hungry, clothe the naked, visit those in bonds, bring the roofless poor into our homes, and attend to every kind of virtue in every way.

Only then shall we fast purely, beginning the holy Forty Days on the thirteenth of the month of Phamenoth, and the seven weeks of the salutary Pascha from the eighteenth of the month of Pharmouthi; we conclude the fasts on the third and tenth of the same Pharmouthi, in the deep evening, according to the evangelical preaching (Matthew 28:20).
We celebrate on the fourth and tenth of the same Pharmouthi, on the sixth brightening Sunday, joining also the seven weeks of the holy Pentecost, according to the arrangement of the divine law.

For thus, being adorned with righteous and good works, we shall inherit the kingdom of the heavens in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom through whom—and with whom—is the glory and the power with the Father, through the Holy Spirit, now and always and unto the ages of ages.
Amen.
